messages:
lia (Support): escalating from tier-2 support: enterprise customer on dedicated pool in us-central1 reporting sudden p99 tail latency spikes and occasional 502s. they say impact started after they turned on streaming function-calls in production ~36h ago. attaching two sample request ids: req_52ff, req_52fa. tagging runtime + infra.

ron (Runtime): thanks. do we have any process-level OOM logs or GPU driver errors? also need model name and if they changed context size.

lia (Support): model: redwood-rt-14b-8q, context configured to 4096 (they occasionally stream >3k tokens). customer pasted agent logs showing repeated errors: 'E inf: device out of memory while allocating 268435456 bytes' and a few 'cudaErrorMemoryAllocation'. they also see slow responses that look like stall-then-retry (clients get partial stream then reconnect).

cleo (Oncall): I'm taking primary. nina, can you check node events and nvidia-smi history for the dedicated pool? ron, can you look at runtime telemetry for KV/attention cache growth?

nina (Infra): pulling events[0K. nodes hosting the pool show GPU driver warnings around 2025-01-22T14:12Z and multiple processes pinned to a single GPU (affinity mismatch). k8s events show pods OOMKilled and SIGTERM around that time. sample nvidia-smi snapshot: 

```
GPU 0: 40GB total, 39.1GB used, processes: inference_worker(38.7GB) python(0.2GB)
GPU 1: 40GB total, 6.2GB used
```

uneven distribution: a hot-process consumes nearly entire GPU, leaving peers underutilized.

oscar (ML): telemetry shows session-level KV sizes growing with streaming calls. avg KV per request increased to 4.8MB for active sessions with function calls vs 1.1MB baseline. also observed repeated re-inserts into the KV when the client reconnects mid-stream 201 multiple small allocations each reconnect.

ron (Runtime): likely combo: aggressive KV growth due to streaming and reconnects + allocator fragmentation from many small allocations + bad GPU packing (session affinity pinned to same GPU). reproduction plan: replay anonymized streaming workload in staging with reconnect patterns and measure retained/resident GPU memory and jemalloc stats. jen (Support) already sanitised payloads? lia?

lia (Support): uploaded replay bundle and customer gave permission to repro in staging for 3 hours. starting now.

devops-bot: replay-job started: replay-20250122-01 on staging-cluster.

ron (Runtime): repro running. early signals: p95 steady ~600ms, p99 ~1.5s. after ~25 minutes we see p99 climb to 6[0Ks and one worker reported cudaErrorMemoryAllocation. grabbing jemalloc stats from the worker: 

```
allocated: 22.4 GB
active: 23.8 GB
resident: 25.6 GB
retained: 2.8 GB
fragmentation_ratio: 11.7%
small_allocs_count: 4.2M
arenas: 56
```

ron (Runtime): fragmentation and rising retained memory. also noticed many small allocations due to session reconnect codepath. additionally, kernel shows no swap pressure so this is purely GPU VRAM exhaustion.

oscar (ML): quick idea: add session-level streaming checkpointing to avoid re-inserting the whole KV on reconnect; also enable dedupe of repeated system prompts. those changes cut median KV delta by ~45% in a local patch.

nina (Infra): infra-level quick wins: rebalance sessions across GPUs on node (round-robin) and change kube scheduler tolerations to avoid packing hot sessions onto a single GPU. we can also cordon the worst nodes and drain them for a controlled restart to reclaim fragmentation.

cleo (Oncall): we need a hotfix bundle we can apply in the next 30 minutes to stop production outages: list proposals.

ron (Runtime): hotfix proposal (canary then roll): 1) enable runtime KV backpressure: cap streaming chunk size to 512 tokens and apply partial KV commit instead of full reinsert on reconnect; 2) set MALLOC_CONF env on inference workers to 'background_thread:true,decay_time:5' to speed decay of unused arenas; 3) add runtime scheduler change to distribute sessions across GPUs more evenly (soft-affinity -> round-robin); 4) fallback route: route sessions to redwood-rt-7b-8q when free GPU < 3GB persist > 20s.

ron (Runtime): commands: 

```
kubectl set env deployment/rt-inference MALLOC_CONF='background_thread:true,decay_time:5' -n dedicated-us-central1
controlplane api update-scheduler --pool dedicated-us-central1 --affinity round_robin
controlplane api set-routing-fallback --pool dedicated-us-central1 --threshold_mb 3072 --duration_s 20 --fallback_model redwood-rt-7b-8q
kubectl apply -f streaming-backpressure.yaml -n dedicated-us-central1
```

nina (Infra): can do canary of MALLOC_CONF on two pods and rebalance scheduler weight for that pool. I'll also throttle pod packing for the pool until we verify.

oscar (ML): patching session manager to partial-commit KV on reconnect, but will gate behind feature flag and enable only for this customer's pool. will push to canary in ~20m.

lia (Support): customer agreed to temporary streaming cap and fallback to smaller model. they prefer minimal downtime.

devops-bot: canary deployment updated: MALLOC_CONF set on pods rt-canary-03, rt-canary-04.

ron (Runtime): canary metrics after 30m: fragmentation down (retained -0.9GB), p99 improved from 9.8s to 2.1s on canaries. KV per-session median dropped from 4.8MB -> 2.6MB with partial commits and backpressure. however, one non-canary node still shows uneven GPU packing.

nina (Infra): started a rolling rebalance and added a scheduler constraint to avoid packing >2 hot sessions per GPU. watching for side effects.

cleo (Oncall): owners and next steps: 
- ron (Runtime): monitor canary for 4h, prepare rollback docs (owner: ron)
- oscar (ML): enable partial-commit KV feature flag for customer pool and run A/B for 12h (owner: oscar)
- nina (Infra): roll scheduler change to other nodes and drain the top-2 fragmented nodes for compaction (owner: nina)
- lia (Support): communicate follow-up and maintenance window for final rollout (owner: lia)

ron (Runtime): will also add an alert rule: if per-GPU retained delta > +800MB in 20m OR p99 increases > 4x with steady p95 -> page oncall and auto-enable KV backpressure for that pool.

oscar (ML): long-term actions: 1) implement streaming reconnect-safe KV merge to avoid re-inserting old state, 2) investigate compressed KV representations per model to reduce VRAM footprint, 3) add hints to SDK for safer reconnect and chunking.

lia (Support): customer reported staging tests look good and accepted the planned rollout tonight at 01:00 UTC. thanking the team.

cleo (Oncall): incident summary for postmortem: root cause = streaming reconnects causing repeated small allocations and KV re-inserts + allocator fragmentation + GPU packing imbalance -> GPU VRAM exhaustion and OOM allocations -> p99 tail spikes. immediate mitigations = streaming backpressure, jemalloc decay tuning, session redistribution, KV partial commit and fallback routing. followups assigned. closing after 12h stable. :white_check_mark:

devops-bot: incident-created: CIR-2025-0072 (severity: high) [0K linked ticket TCK-22334.
